page: Microsoft Azure M64m is a memory-intensive server instance belonging to the MS family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical Intel Xeon 8280M cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz and includes 38 MB of L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 1792.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 28.0 GB per core. Local storage is bundled with a capacity of 7340 GB, and there are no onboard GPUs.

Benchmark data reveals a clear performance tradeoff between single-core and multi-core workloads. Single-core performance is consistently limited, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression all scoring in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core and multi-threaded performance is more robust. The instance achieves average ratings in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and Passmark CPU tests. Notably, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performs strongly, ranking in the top 25%. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks, along with Passmark memory scores, fall within the average range.

Given its massive memory capacity and bundled 7340 GB local storage, the M64m is designed for memory-intensive workloads such as large-scale databases, in-memory caching, and data warehousing. Redis SET operations and database operations perform at average levels. However, its weak single-core execution and poor text generation speeds for large language models make it less suitable for compute-bound single-threaded tasks or real-time LLM inference. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the high resource density of RAM and local storage provides a specialized platform where massive memory footprints are required, though users trade off raw single-core CPU speed.
